design_promise: The upper keep buys time and information; the ground keep converts that time into interception, recovery, or refuge.

layout.principle: The two layers are one keep, not two separate boards. Every upper placement has a ground dependency and every ground response has an information or access relationship to the upper layer.

vertical_connections.purpose: Lets defenders and repair runners move between the tower and ground response space.
vertical_connections.failure_effect: Ground response time increases and the tower becomes isolated.

vertical_connections.purpose: Connects wall defense to the primary ground entry.
vertical_connections.failure_effect: Wall defenders cannot reinforce the gate quickly.

vertical_connections.purpose: Carries warnings and commander orders across floors.
vertical_connections.failure_effect: Forecasts remain visible but response timing and morale recovery are reduced.

floor_roles.name: Walls and Towers
floor_roles.purpose: Warning, ranged pressure, route control, and early intervention.
floor_roles.readability_rule: The player must see which ground room supplies each upper piece and which approach each piece can observe or cover.

floor_roles.name: Ground Floor and Yard
floor_roles.purpose: Interception, movement, repair, reserves, supplies, morale, and refuge.
floor_roles.readability_rule: The player must see where a reserve can move, where a repair station can reach, and which upper alerts can be answered.

upper_units.purpose: Reveals enemy doctrine and likely landing or approach points.
Carries alerts from a tower to connected ground rooms.
Applies steady pressure to enemies outside the walls.
Delivers a powerful, slow attack along a declared approach lane.
Reveals climbers and burrowers while making the outer approach legible.
Reduces breach damage to an adjacent wall or tower attachment.

ground_units.purpose: Holds a narrow gate, corridor, or stair landing.
Protects adjacent ground units and stabilizes a selected boundary.
Restores damaged rooms, stairs, wall supports, or equipment during recovery.
Controls open yard space and punishes enemies that land inside the walls.
Carries repair kits, orders, or evacuation supplies between rooms and floors.
Coordinates the response when alerts cross between upper and ground layers.
Supports an upper heavy weapon by protecting its reload window and ground approach.
Protects civilians and essential supplies during a scarred defense or evacuation.

pack_layer_identity.cross_floor_benefit: A narrow upper approach feeds a ground-floor holding lane.
pack_layer_identity.cross_floor_risk: If the stair or gate connection fails, the pike line becomes isolated.

pack_layer_identity.cross_floor_benefit: Ground repair keeps wall and tower pieces from becoming permanent losses.
pack_layer_identity.cross_floor_risk: The repair room becomes a high-value sapper target.

pack_layer_identity.cross_floor_benefit: Upper visibility and ground denial shape the same approach space.
pack_layer_identity.cross_floor_risk: Fire can protect the yard while making a friendly route unsafe.

pack_layer_identity.cross_floor_benefit: Information becomes a ground response rather than a passive bonus.
pack_layer_identity.cross_floor_risk: If the signal chain is cut, the player has knowledge without coordination.

pack_layer_identity.cross_floor_benefit: The upper boundary protects a controlled ground retreat.
pack_layer_identity.cross_floor_risk: Sealing the wall can trap or disconnect the ground reserve.

pack_layer_identity.cross_floor_benefit: Signals direct movement and supplies across the keep.
pack_layer_identity.cross_floor_risk: A blocked lane turns the mobility doctrine into stranded pieces.

pack_layer_identity.cross_floor_benefit: Alerts and morale survive one damaged room when the relay is redundant.
pack_layer_identity.cross_floor_risk: The pack is indirect and weak if the player has no actual response units.

pack_layer_identity.cross_floor_benefit: The upper weapon creates a firing window while the ground team reloads and protects the approach.
pack_layer_identity.cross_floor_risk: Large footprint and reload dependency make it poor against bypasses.

enemy_floor_tests.upper_response: Buy time and reveal the approach.
enemy_floor_tests.ground_response: Hold the lane or deploy a reserve.

enemy_floor_tests.pressure: Repair rooms, stairs, signal relays, and supply dependencies.
enemy_floor_tests.upper_response: Expose the sapper route and protect the relay.
enemy_floor_tests.ground_response: Intercept or repair after the hit.

enemy_floor_tests.pressure: Wall landing and bypass of the gate.
enemy_floor_tests.upper_response: Detection, watchfire, and denial before landing.
enemy_floor_tests.ground_response: Respond in the yard or stair landing.

enemy_floor_tests.pressure: Area damage across a wall, tower, and nearby ground room.
enemy_floor_tests.upper_response: Ballista or delay buys a firing window.
enemy_floor_tests.ground_response: Repair, evacuate, or preserve a smaller keep.

enemy_floor_tests.pressure: Smoke obscures towers and cuts signal clarity.
enemy_floor_tests.upper_response: Redundant watch and alternate signal paths.
enemy_floor_tests.ground_response: Operate with partial information and preserve morale.

enemy_floor_tests.pressure: Interior emergence away from the wall.
enemy_floor_tests.upper_response: Warning and map markers if detected.

new_tracks.name: Vertical Readiness
new_tracks.purpose: Unlocks better information and movement between floors.

nodes.choice_created: assign defenders to a stair before the wave
protect a signal chain instead of adding another weapon
keep a ground reserve ready for an upper breach

new_tracks.name: Layered Recovery
new_tracks.purpose: Makes a damaged floor survivable without erasing the cost of a breach.

nodes.choice_created: repair a wall before rebuilding a room
maintain a smaller but connected keep
turn a tower loss into a controlled evacuation

guardrails: The upper floor must not be a universally safer version of the ground floor.
Every upper piece has at least one ground dependency.
Every ground response has a visible access or information requirement.
A lost tower, wall segment, or stair can reduce options without automatically ending the run.
The first vertical slice uses visibility, access, and support as the only cross-floor rules.
